page: Vultr vhf-2c-4gb is a virtual server in the High Frequency Compute family. It features an x86_64 Intel processor with 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core via hyperthreading, operating with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and includes 128 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include a GPU. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1873.78 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1456.0. Multi-core performance is weaker, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3596.49 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2405.0, reflecting the shared CPU allocation. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with uncached read speeds at 22.81 GB/sec and write speeds at 12.89 GB/sec, both falling into the poor performance category. Single-threaded gzip compression is a strong point at 32.63 GB/sec, while database operations and Redis SET operations perform poorly.

This server offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads that benefit from high-frequency single-core performance but do not require sustained multi-core execution or high memory bandwidth. Due to the shared CPU allocation and limited memory capacity, it is best suited for lightweight applications, basic web serving, single-threaded utility scripts, and development environments rather than heavy database or memory-intensive production workloads.
